clue.text: A singular feat for a clubman?

definitions.text: A singular feat for a clubman?

parts.words: A singular feat for a clubman?
parts.note: a golfer swinging a club who sinks the ball from the tee with just one stroke achieves a rare single-shot feat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubman' suggests a member of a gentlemen's club, but here it is a golfer wielding a club, and 'singular' points at a single stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's ace, holing the ball with the tee shot, is a celebrated rarity on the course.

clue.text: They may be holy to take in the vicar

definitions.text: They may be holy to take in the vicar

parts.words: They may be holy to take in the vicar
parts.note: a clergyman is ordained into ministry by taking up the sacred commission described with the word 'holy', so the vicar is the one who takes them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like housing or deceiving the vicar; it is the vicar who took these, in the phrase for being ordained.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ordained is called taking holy ones of these, the commissions that make someone a priest.

clue.text: Hemingway went after an eagle, by the way

indicators.note: by means beside, so the second piece sits next to the first

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword regular
ST, short for street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: The novelist set off in pursuit of an eagle along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went after' is only a link, and 'by the way' looks like an aside but gives ST, the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist's first name was this, as in Ernest Miller Hemingway.

clue.text: Pinned down by attack, it's reported

annotationWithheld.why: Pinned down by attack, it's reported (6): 'Pinned down' defines NAILED, but no parse found makes 'by attack, it's reported' yield NAILED as a homophone or second definition
annotationWithheld.clue: Pinned down by attack, it's reported

clue.text: The curious yen vita had for simplicity

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters of yen vita are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A strange longing that Vita felt was for the simple life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' looks like it describes the yen; it signals the anagram of YENVITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless innocence and lack of guile are what simplicity means in a person.

clue.text: For both parties, bill must include one exchange rate

indicators.note: must include means the bill has to hold the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a bill as written, an account or invoice
A is one, as in a single item

indicators.note: exchange means swap round, so the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a two-sided deal, the invoice should state the currency conversion rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a demand for payment and 'exchange rate' a currency term; 'exchange' is in fact the anagram signal acting on 'rate' alone, giving TERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-sided agreement involves and binds each side equally.

clue.text: He may sit on the fence — or on a hill!

definitions.text: He may sit on the fence — or on a hill!

parts.words: He may sit on the fence — or on a hill!
parts.note: one who sits on the fence cannot decide; split up, the answer reads as ..., a tor being a rocky hill

explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a craggy hilltop, found on Dartmoor in England. The joke reads the answer as the words 'he sit a tor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undecided, wavering between two sides, is said to sit on the fence.

clue.text: Held short altercation on the doorstep

indicators.note: an altercation is a noisy quarrel, so the letters of held short are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A brief quarrel was held on someone's front step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altercation' looks like part of the story but signals an anagram of HELDSHORT.
explanation.definitionFit: The sill at the entrance of a house, the step you cross going in, is this.

clue.text: Scientifically advanced — snag is, needing energy source

indicators.note: needing means the snag takes in the extra letter it lacks, put inside it

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

indicators.note: source means the beginning, so only the first letter of energy is used

explanation.surface: The trouble with new technology is that it needs a power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' takes E, the start of 'energy', which goes into HITCH after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for high technology, describing advanced electronic and scientific gadgetry.

clue.text: Face make-up?

parts.note: not cosmetics but a face built up from a kit of features, as police assemble a suspect's likeness from a witness's description

explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics; it means making up a face from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A police composite picture of a wanted person, pieced together from separate features.

clue.text: A case for making appointment around four

indicators.note: around means the appointment's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a date is an appointment or engagement
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone argues that arranging a meeting is justified with four people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case' looks like a legal case or argument; it is the grammatical case, and 'for making' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the case of the indirect object, as in Latin, is one of the noun cases.

clue.text: Tempestuous character, lacking love, thrived with Edward

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so one letter of the character's name is dropped

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest
love is zero in tennis, written O
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A stormy figure, out of romance, did well alongside a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempestuous' looks like a description of temper; it names Shakespeare's play The Tempest. Dropping the final O leaves PROSPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or succeed financially is to do very well, and the past tense matches.

clue.text: Europe's achievement, to keep Passover

indicators.note: to keep means the phrase holds the answer within its letters, running across the words

explanation.surface: A European triumph is observed during the Jewish festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'Europe's' into the start of 'achievement'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew name for the Jewish spring festival commemorating the Exodus from Egypt.

clue.text: Little arch over the line in Surrey

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a camber is a slight arch or convex curve, as on a road surface
a ley is a line, as in the ley lines said to join ancient sites

explanation.surface: A small curved bridge crosses a railway line somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBERLEY is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This town lies in the English county, near the Berkshire and Hampshire borders.

clue.text: Truce possible if a fighting force is on the ball

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the earlier pieces sit on top of the next

parts.note: an arm of the services, such as the army or navy, is a fighting force
taken as written
a tice is an old cricketing term for a yorker, a ball pitched at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: A ceasefire might come about if an army is alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ball' looks like the idiom for alert; it is TICE, a dated cricket word for a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal halt to fighting agreed by both sides, as on 11 November 1918.

clue.text: One dictionary reversed diagram of symbol

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: reversed means the dictionary's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a graph is a diagram plotting data

explanation.surface: A lone dictionary flipped a chart showing a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns OED into DEO.
explanation.definitionFit: A written character standing for an idea rather than a sound, as in Chinese script, is a symbol.

clue.text: Ta-ta — must run!

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored when the ball passes the batsman without being hit is one of these extras

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye in a hurry because they have to dash.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a short farewell and the cricket extra run taken when the ball is missed.

clue.text: Pray to be good

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run on unbroken across 'be good' is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A plea to behave well.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead or entreat earnestly, as in 'pray, tell me', is the same as to implore.

clue.text: Not a very long time in this case

definitions.text: Not a very long time in this case

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter given by the word a is left out

parts.note: an aeon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A remark that something did not take ages here.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling AEON loses its A; the result is still a very long time, which is the joke of 'Not ... in this case'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortened spelling still denotes an age of geological length, so the clue's 'not' is ironic.

clue.text: Shorten a nasal bone

parts.note: the bridge of the nose is its bony upper part

explanation.surface: Someone is told to trim a bone in the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text by cutting it down is to make it shorter.

clue.text: Enjoying lucky streak over bridge, perhaps?

parts.note: on can mean over, as something resting on top
a bridge roll is a small soft finger-shaped bread roll, so a bridge is an example of a roll

explanation.surface: A card player asks whether their winning run came at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game; it is a bridge roll, a soft finger-shaped bread roll popular in Britain at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a run of successes is an idiom from gambling luck continuing.

clue.text: Soldier getting new spirit

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is given a fresh lease of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like morale; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear juniper-flavoured liquor is a spirit, a strong distilled drink.

clue.text: Make one's mark

parts.note: making an impact on people and literally stamping a mark into a surface are both meant here

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds figurative, but the answer also means to stamp a mark physically, as a seal does in wax.
explanation.definitionFit: To win admiration, or to press a design into a soft material, both fit making a mark.

clue.text: A native of Brighton, not Ghana!

definitions.text: A native of Brighton, not Ghana!

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters for Ghana are removed from the town's name

parts.note: GH is the international code for Ghana

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that a person comes from the English seaside town, not the African country.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON, an English south-coast resort, loses its G and H to leave the answer, and a Brighton native is indeed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Britain, such as someone born in an English seaside town, is a native of that nation.

clue.text: A hard way to get behind

parts.note: stern means hard or severe

explanation.surface: A tough route to getting to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way to get' is the link to the definition: in sailing, a ship going this way moves backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: At or towards the rear of a ship is the nautical sense of lying back.

clue.text: Firm to feature Indian port

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A company wants to appear in an Indian harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' looks like a verb, to appear in; it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Kerala coast, now Kochi, is a major Indian harbour.

clue.text: Nothing has come up to clear singer

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: Nothing emerged that would vindicate the vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has come up' turns NIL into LIN. 'singer' looks like a vocalist; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small finch is a songbird, prized for its warbling.

clue.text: Pauline perhaps relating to preachers

definitions.meaning: Pauline means of St Paul, one of the early missionaries of the church
relating to the twelve sent out by Jesus to preach the gospel

explanation.surface: A woman called Pauline may be connected with preaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers the twelve disciples and Paul, missionaries sent out to preach.

clue.text: Weary once more, so go to bed

parts.note: re means again, as in redo
to tire is to weary or become exhausted

explanation.surface: Feeling exhausted all over again, someone decides to turn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing for the night to sleep is the sense of turning in.

clue.text: Call out?

parts.note: not shouting but ringing a number, the instrument used to make a call going out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call out' suggests shouting or summoning; read as a call going out on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the device used to ring people, so it makes outgoing calls.

clue.text: Two ways to head after break-out

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south, ways to travel
E and S are compass directions, east and south, ways to travel
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Two routes lead to the headland following a jailbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a verb, to travel; it is a headland. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight from captivity, getting free from prison, is a break-out.

clue.text: An immoral act — one tiny perversion — such stupidity!

parts.note: a sin is an immoral act
I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: perversion means twisting out of shape, so the letters of tiny are distorted

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a wicked deed and a small depravity as utterly foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversion' turns TINY into NITY. 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Silliness or utter foolishness is the same as stupidity.
